gloss: to lack, to be short of

definitions.gloss: to lack, to be short of, to want for
definitions.explanation: To be in a state of not having enough of something. Most commonly used in the negative form 事欠かない, meaning "to have no shortage of" or "to never lack for."

examples.japanese: {話題|わだい}に{事欠|ことか}かない。
examples.english: There is no shortage of things to talk about.

examples.japanese: あの{人|ひと}は{問題|もんだい}に{事欠|ことか}かない{人|ひと}だ。
examples.english: That person is someone who never runs out of problems.

examples.japanese: {食|た}べるものにも{事欠|ことか}くような{生活|せいかつ}をしていた{時代|じだい}があった。
examples.english: There was a time when people lived lacking even food to eat.

notes:
USAGE:
{事欠|ことか}く is most frequently used in the negative form {事欠|ことか}かない, meaning "to have no shortage of" or "to never lack." The affirmative form {事欠|ことか}く (to lack) is rarer and sounds more literary.

The pattern ～に{事欠|ことか}かない means "there is no shortage of ~."

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～に{事欠|ことか}かない: to have no shortage of
- ～にも{事欠|ことか}く: to lack even ~
- {話題|わだい}に{事欠|ことか}かない: never at a loss for topics
- {例|れい}に{事欠|ことか}かない: to have no shortage of examples
